summary: The control blocks the exact 2026-08-21 incident shape end-to-end, verified independently against the live hook (not only via the committed tests). No secrets are handled, no injection or ReDoS surface, and the override cannot be self-granted from inside a Bash command string. Six findings, none blocking: one MEDIUM audit/UX defect inherited from ENF-16's wording, one MEDIUM under-documented coverage gap, two LOW, two INFO.

findings.title: The documented override syntax produces an UNAUDITED silent allow instead of an audited override
findings.detail: The block message says: `Override: LEO_ALLOW_ONE_OFF_IMPORT="<ticket: reason>" <your command>`. That inline-prefix form cannot work, for two independent reasons. (a) An inline shell assignment is part of the command STRING only; it never enters the hook's own process env, so the override branch can never fire from it. (b) The prefix also moves `node` off the operative boundary, so OPERATIVE_ONE_OFF_IMPORT_RE does not match at all - decideOneOffBareImport returns {matched:false}, the hook writes NO audit row, and the command is silently allowed. Live-verified: exit=0, no ENF-18 stderr. Net effect: an operator who follows the printed instruction converts an 'audited override with a recorded reason' into an 'unaudited pass'. The security posture of the override itself is CORRECT (an agent cannot self-grant - separately verified, see independent_verification #2); this is a documentation/audit-coverage defect, not a privilege defect.
findings.pre_existing: ENF-16 ships the identical wording for LEO_ALLOW_NO_VERIFY (pre-tool-enforce.cjs:1572), so this is an inherited house pattern, NOT a regression introduced by this PR.
findings.recommendation: Change the ENF-18 message to name a channel that actually reaches the hook: the `.claude/settings.json` `env` block, or exporting the var before launching the session. Optionally also extend the operative boundary to tolerate leading `VAR=value` assignments so a prefixed command still MATCHES and blocks-with-guidance rather than passing silently. Consider the same correction for ENF-16 in a follow-up.

findings.title: The stated KNOWN GAP is narrower than the measured gap set
findings.detail: The header comment documents only ONE gap (dynamically-built import specifiers). Measured bypasses that are ACCIDENTAL command shapes rather than adversarial obfuscation, and that the comment does not mention: (1) any env prefix - `NODE_NO_WARNINGS=1 node -e "import('<dangerous>')"` is ALLOWED (live-verified exit=0); (2) wrappers - `npx node ...`, `timeout 30 node ...`, `nohup node ...`; (3) non-node runtimes - `npx tsx -e ...`, ts-node, bun, and notably `npx vitest run <file>` where the TEST FILE imports the one-off (relevant given this SD is named TEST-FIXTURE-LANE); (4) indirection - write a wrapper .mjs that imports the one-off, then `node wrapper.mjs`; (5) an absolute Windows path or a `file:///C:/...` specifier - the ':' is outside the path character class, and file:// is the form Node REQUIRES for an absolute ESM specifier on win32; (6) an uppercase path on a case-insensitive filesystem (no `i` flag). This does not make the control worthless - it closes the exact literal shape that caused the incident, which is the highest-frequency accidental form, and the fail-open-by-default design means every gap degrades to today's status quo, never worse. The issue is that the comment currently reads as a stronger claim than the code supports.
findings.recommendation: Broaden the KNOWN GAP paragraph (and the PRD residual-risk note) to enumerate env/wrapper prefixes, non-node runtimes, file-indirection, absolute/file-URL specifiers, and case sensitivity. Optional cheap hardening: allow `(?:[A-Za-z_]\w*=(?:"[^"]*"|'[^']*'|\S*)\s+)*` before the runner token and widen `node\b` to `(?:node|npx|tsx|ts-node|bun|deno)\b`.

findings.title: Drift workflow path filter omits *.js while the generator scans it
findings.detail: .github/workflows/one-off-mutate-key-manifest-drift.yml triggers on scripts/one-off/**/*.mjs and **/*.cjs, but the generator's SCAN_EXTENSIONS includes '.js'. A future dangerous scripts/one-off/foo.js could therefore merge without the drift check running, leaving the manifest stale - and a stale manifest is exactly the fail-open the workflow's own header comment says it exists to prevent (not_in_dangerous_manifest -> allow). Measured impact today is nil: 1 tracked .js file in scripts/one-off, 0 .js manifest entries (all 45 are .mjs). Also note the workflow is pull_request-only, so a direct push to main would not run it.
findings.recommendation: Add `- 'scripts/one-off/**/*.js'` to the workflow paths. One line.

findings.title: Textual mutate signature misses .rpc()/raw-SQL/helper-mediated writes
findings.detail: Dangerousness = /SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY/ AND /\.(insert|update|upsert|delete)\s*\(/. Measured on the current corpus (1,112 tracked one-off scripts): 12 files hold the service-role key and call .rpc( with NO CRUD method, and 126 hold the key with no CRUD at all. A write performed through .rpc(), raw SQL / psql, or an imported helper that owns the client is invisible to the classifier, so those files can never be blocked by ENF-18. This is honestly disclosed in the generator header ('a coarse, fast, precomputed CLASSIFIER, not a security proof; false positives just cost an unnecessary block, false negatives are the real risk and are documented as a known gap'), and the direction of error is safe-by-design (conservative on parse failure -> treated as dangerous).
findings.recommendation: Optional widening: add `\.rpc\s*\(` to MUTATE_RE (adds <=12 entries, requires bumping RATCHET_MAX from 45 in the same PR). Defer is acceptable - this is a defense-in-depth net, not a security proof.

findings.title: Fail-open and allow/override audit rows are fire-and-forget
findings.detail: On the non-block paths the auditPromise is deliberately not awaited (falls through), matching ENF-15/16/17. main() ends at process.exit(0) (pre-tool-enforce.cjs:1735) with a comment saying that form was chosen specifically so fire-and-forget writes survive, so the pattern is established and intentional. It does mean a `manifest_unreadable_fail_open` event - the one fail-open that could silently disarm the control for a genuinely dangerous file - is best-effort recorded rather than guaranteed.
findings.recommendation: If manifest-staleness observability matters, await ONLY the manifest_unreadable_fail_open decision path (bounded by the existing 1000ms auditAndExit race). Not required for this handoff.

findings.title: Manifest tamper resistance and the --root/--check flag wart
findings.detail: TRUST BOUNDARY - ACCEPTABLE: the manifest is a repo file under the same review/merge process as code. Removing an entry by hand is caught by the CI drift check, which regenerates from source rather than trusting the committed file. Adding a fake main-guard to a source file to drop it from the manifest is caught only by human review of that source diff - but anyone who can do that can already edit the one-off script itself, so the guard adds no new attack surface. The ratchet test bounds GROWTH (<=45) but not shrinkage, which is the correct asymmetry (shrinkage = guard retrofits). The extra ratchet assertions (dangerous_count matches entry count; every key exists on disk; every key starts with scripts/one-off/) are meaningful anti-hand-edit checks. FLAG WART: `--check --root <dir>` scans the fixture root but compares against the module-constant MANIFEST_PATH (the real committed manifest), so the two are never comparable. Harmless for CI (which never passes --root) and the test names it 'drift by construction', but the flag combination is misleading and could mislead a future maintainer into thinking a fixture drift-check is meaningful.
findings.recommendation: Optionally make MANIFEST_PATH root-relative when --root is supplied, or reject the --check + --root combination.

detailed_analysis.scope: ENF-18 bare-import-of-dangerous-one-off-script guard: scripts/hooks/lib/one-off-bare-import.cjs, scripts/lint/generate-one-off-mutate-key-manifest.mjs, scripts/lint/one-off-mutate-key-manifest.json, scripts/hooks/pre-tool-enforce.cjs (+31), .github/workflows/one-off-mutate-key-manifest-drift.yml, 4 test files

independent_verification.check: live hook blocks the incident shape
independent_verification.method: spawned scripts/hooks/pre-tool-enforce.cjs as a real subprocess with a PreToolUse Bash payload naming a real manifest entry (scripts/one-off/_audit-dual-detection-clusters.mjs)
independent_verification.result: exit=2, stderr contains '[ENF-18] BLOCKED' + the target path. Control is live and not dead-by-construction.

independent_verification.check: override cannot be granted from within the command string
independent_verification.method: live hook run with command `LEO_ALLOW_ONE_OFF_IMPORT="QF-1"; node -e "import('<dangerous>')"` and LEO_ALLOW_ONE_OFF_IMPORT deleted from the hook's own env
independent_verification.result: exit=2 ENF-18 BLOCKED. An inline shell assignment never reaches the hook process env, so an agent cannot self-grant. Correct security property. The only working grant channels are the .claude/settings.json `env` block (which exists and is inherited by the hook) or exporting before launching the session.

independent_verification.method: direct calls to decideOneOffBareImport() with a real manifest entry
independent_verification.result: block on: baseline `node -e "import('./X')"`, no-./ prefix, `await import`, `require(...)`, after `&&`, extra spaces inside import(, backtick specifier. Correctly allows direct execution and grep/cat mentions. Bypass set recorded in findings F2.

independent_verification.method: OPERATIVE_ONE_OFF_IMPORT_RE.test() against 1k/5k/20k/100k-char near-miss (repeating path-segment) and long-filler inputs
independent_verification.result: 0.09ms @1k -> 0.50ms @100k (near-miss); 0.005ms -> 0.19ms (long filler). Linear, not exponential. The path atom classes ([\w.-]+ vs [/\\]+) are disjoint so there is no catastrophic-backtracking ambiguity. NOT a ReDoS risk.

The generator regex-matches the IDENTIFIER 'SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY' in source text; it never reads the value. The manifest carries only repo-relative paths plus a static reason string - no code excerpts, no credentials, no env values. Clean.

execFileSync('git', [...]) with an args array and a `--` pathspec separator (no shell). `--root` is path.resolve()d and used only as cwd / path.join base. The hook module does pure string+regex work: no exec, no eval, no dynamic require of caller-controlled paths. No injection surface.

independent_verification.check: the incident file is legitimately absent from the manifest
independent_verification.result: TRUE NEGATIVE, not a classifier miss: the file now carries an `isDirectRun` main-guard (process.argv[1] === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) plus a default-dry-run --apply requirement from the prior remediation SD. It is correctly classified as guarded/not-dangerous.

independent_verification.method: npx vitest run on all 4 new test files
independent_verification.result: 31/31 pass in 2.46s. `--check` has BOTH a true-negative (real repo, exit 0) and a drift case (exit 1). Fixtures are created under os.tmpdir(); no stray files landed in scripts/one-off/ and the worktree is porcelain-clean after the run.

security_checklist.authentication_mechanism: N/A - no auth surface in this diff
security_checklist.authorization_model: Override grant is process-env-scoped and cannot be set by the gated command string (live-verified). Correct.
security_checklist.sensitive_data: None handled. Only the string 'SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY' is matched as an identifier; no values read, stored, or logged.
security_checklist.input_validation: Command string is treated as untrusted text and only regex-tested; typeof/length guards present; no path is ever resolved, opened, or executed from the matched value.
security_checklist.output_sanitization: The blocked target path is echoed to stderr. It is constrained by the regex to [\w.-/]+ under scripts/one-off/, so no control-character or ANSI injection into the terminal is possible.
security_checklist.sql_injection: N/A - no SQL in this diff
security_checklist.secrets_in_code: None. No hardcoded credentials; no .env reads added.
security_checklist.redos: Measured linear, sub-millisecond at 100KB input. Not a risk.
security_checklist.fail_open_correctness: Fail-open triggers only on regex non-match, unreadable/corrupt manifest, or an internal throw. For the exact incident shape with a well-formed manifest the control BLOCKS (live-verified). The one fail-open that could defeat the control for a NEW dangerous file - manifest staleness - is covered by the CI drift check (SEC-F3 notes its *.js path gap) and the ratchet test.

detailed_analysis.final_recommendation: APPROVE for EXEC-TO-PLAN. No blocking security defects. SEC-F1 (fix the override message to name .claude/settings.json env) and SEC-F3 (add *.js to the workflow paths) are two-line changes worth folding into this PR; SEC-F2 (broaden the KNOWN GAP comment to match the measured gap set) is a comment-only edit that keeps the control's self-description honest. SEC-F4/F5/F6 are acceptable as residual risk.
